results.note: All counts match Results paragraph 1 and Table 2: 169,103 men, 2,857,312 person-years (16.9 per man, so 'about 17' holds), 10,928 deaths, 124,256 never-users (73.5%), 39,156 exclusive current (23.2%), 5,691 former. Exposure recorded at baseline only.

Every aHR, interval and death count matches Table 3 and Results paragraph 2 (reference never-users of tobacco; adjusted for attained age and BMI). Former-user CVD and other-cause intervals include 1. Table 3 prints death counts only, no rates or person-years.

All numbers and p values match Table 3. Only fix: the duration and amount ratios did not name their comparison group; Table 3 note c says exclusive current snus users only, reference never-users of tobacco. Added. No number changes.
results.corrected_extracted: Among men who currently used snus and no other tobacco, against never-users of tobacco, by years of snus use at baseline, all-cause aHR rose from 1.08 (0.88–1.32) under 5 years to 1.29 (1.20–1.38) at 15 years or more (p for trend 0.001); cardiovascular and other-cause deaths showed the same pattern (p for trend 0.001 each), cancer did not (0.11). Few deaths sit in the shorter categories (13 cardiovascular deaths under 5 years). By weekly amount, all-cause aHR was 1.28 (under 4 cans), 1.17 (4 to 6) and 1.37 (7 or more), p for trend 0.09; the cardiovascular ratio was highest in the lightest group (1.44, 1.18, 1.17; p for trend 0.03), the other-cause ratio highest in the heaviest (1.24, 1.18, 1.65; p for trend 0.001), and cancer showed no pattern (p for trend 0.22). The abstract says risks did not increase with weekly amount; the trends by amount differ by cause.

results.note: All figures match Table 4; 1,233/1,410 = 87% and 6,116/9,272 = 66% check. But 'raised the ratios' is wrong for other causes: 1.37 in Table 3 became 1.34 (0.97–1.86). The text says only cardiovascular and cancer were inflated. Reworded.
results.corrected_extracted: Leaving out the Construction Worker Cohort raised the all-cause, cardiovascular and cancer ratios for current snus use against never use of tobacco: all-cause 1.42 (1.21–1.66), cardiovascular 1.39 (1.05–1.84), cancer 1.52 (1.15–1.99); the other-cause ratio was 1.34 (0.97–1.86), against 1.37 in the full analysis, and its interval now includes 1. That cohort supplied 87% of the deaths in the current snus group (1,233 of 1,410) and 66% of those in the never-used group (6,116 of 9,272) (editors' arithmetic from Tables 3 and 4). Follow-up capped at 10 years: all-cause 1.34 (1.21–1.48), cancer 1.24 (1.02–1.52), other causes 1.57 (1.35–1.83), but cardiovascular 1.13 (0.93–1.38), no longer distinguishable from no difference; the authors say the cardiovascular result should be read with caution because of this inconsistency. Extra adjustment for education, alcohol and physical activity in six cohorts (158 snus-group deaths): all-cause 1.46 (1.22–1.75), cardiovascular 1.56 (1.14–2.14), cancer 1.51 (1.12–2.03), other causes 1.20 (0.83–1.72).

results.note: Table 2 values match. But alcohol and education percentages are only within cohorts that recorded them (table note a; Methods): the Construction Workers Cohort is left out, and it supplies most deaths. Qualifier added. Age and BMI cover all men.
results.corrected_extracted: The current snus group was younger (mean age 29 against 38 years), drank more (37.9% in the highest alcohol tertile against 20.2%) and more often had 10 to 12 years of education (52.6% against 38.7%) than men who never used tobacco (the alcohol and education percentages are within the cohorts that recorded them, which leaves out the Construction Workers Cohort); body mass index was similar (24.1 against 24.6). The authors name residual confounding and a single baseline measurement of exposure as weaknesses, and describe their findings as supporting an association, with public-health relevance if it is causal. Their suggested explanations (nicotine effects on blood vessels and heart rhythm, tumour promotion, poorer cancer survival, alcohol-linked injury and violence, risk-taking) were not tested in these data.

results.note: Funders, no-role statement and 'None declared' match. 'The authors include those investigators' is not printed anywhere: Methods says only that each cohort's principal investigator provided individual participant data. Clause removed; Methods added to the locator.

results.note: Every figure and certainty grade matches Table 1 and its note. The table gives the 27-year pancreas CI as 1.2–3.3 where the text says 1.2–3.6, as the anchor states. 163,412 = 124,256 + 39,156 (Byhamre Table 2), so same analysis.

Numbers match 3.1.4 and Table 1. No comparison group was named: current snus users at baseline against never users of tobacco; the pooled HR 1.07 is a sensitivity analysis restricted to never smokers. Both added; no number changes.
results.corrected_extracted: Pancreatic cancer in the Construction Workers Cohort, in current snus users at baseline against never users of tobacco, varied with the length of follow-up: HR 1.98 (0.97–4.03, 4 exposed cases) to 1994, 2.1 (1.2–3.6, 18 cases) to 2004, 1.34 (0.90–1.99, 31 cases) to 2013; the pooled nine-cohort analysis (36 years, follow-up to 2013, 41 exposed cases), a sensitivity analysis restricted to never smokers, gave HR 1.07 (0.77–1.50), graded very low. In that pooled analysis two thirds of participants and 72% of cases or deaths came from the Construction Workers Cohort.

results.note: Numbers match 3.1.5 and Table 1. Added the missing comparison group (exclusive current snus users against never users of tobacco). 1.38 to 1.10 is a 20.3% fall, so the authors' 'almost 20%' became 'about 20%'.
results.corrected_extracted: Rectal cancer in exclusive current snus users against never users of tobacco: HR 1.38 (1.07–1.77, 73 exposed cases) at 27 years of follow-up in nine pooled cohorts; combining the non-construction cohorts with a 10-years-longer follow-up of the Construction Workers Cohort gave HR 1.10 (0.91–1.34), a drop of about 20% in the point estimate. Colon cancer HR 1.02 to 1.08 and anal cancer 0.61 (0.07–5.07, 1 case) showed no clear difference.

results.note: Figures match 3.1.1 and 3.1.6–3.1.9. But HR 2.3 (0.7–8.3, 5 cases) is not 'close to no difference or lower'; qualified, group named. Hodgkin lymphoma after 30+ years, IRR 3.78 (1.23–11.60, 4 cases), was left out; added.
results.corrected_extracted: Snus only against no tobacco, estimates close to no difference or lower (except one high but imprecise estimate, noted below): oral cancer (pooled 9 cohorts HR 0.93, 0.59–1.44, 25 exposed cases; a third study of oral and pharyngeal cancers combined, in never-smoking daily users, HR 2.3, 0.7–8.3, 5 cases, whose interval includes no difference), lung cancer RR 0.8 (0.4–1.3, 15 cases), non-Hodgkin lymphoma incidence rate ratio 0.77 (0.59–1.01), Hodgkin lymphoma 0.88 (0.49–1.58; in men who used snus for over 30 years 3.78, 1.23–11.60, 4 cases), leukaemias and myeloma 0.81 to 1.24, all melanoma 0.65 (0.52–0.82); the lymphoma, leukaemia and melanoma results were not graded because they were given as incidence rate ratios.

results.note: All HRs and counts match 3.1.11–3.1.14. Added the comparison groups the source names (never users of tobacco; never users of snus; patients who never used tobacco). It also omits colorectal cancer-specific HR 1.00 (0.66–1.53, 29 deaths).
results.corrected_extracted: Mortality: a pooled Swedish analysis of eight cohorts (the Byhamre et al., 2021 study, named as the source of the cancer-specific row in Table 1 and matching it in figures, so counted once) gave, for exclusive current snus users against never users of tobacco, all-cause HR 1.28 (1.20–1.35) and cancer-specific HR 1.12 (1.00–1.26); a separate cohort not in that analysis gave HR 1.23 (1.09–1.40) for all-cause and 1.28 (0.96–1.69) for cancer death in never-smoking men who had ever used snus, against never users of snus. After a cancer diagnosis in construction workers, against patients who never used tobacco, total mortality HR 1.13 (1.05–1.20) and cancer death HR 1.15 (1.05–1.26); after prostate cancer, overall HR 1.19 (1.04–1.37) and prostate cancer death HR 1.24 (1.03–1.49); after colorectal cancer, overall HR 1.16 (0.89–1.50), and 1.89 (1.21–2.94, 22 deaths) when the construction cohort was left out.

results.note: Matches the Discussion opening paragraph and Section 5. 'Moderate' and 'low' follow the authors' wording rule (Methods 2.6) and Table 1; women, 'very uncertain' and the hazard conclusion are as printed. No advice wording.

results.note: Matches 2.3, 4.1, 4.2 and the conflict statement; page has no funding statement (searched). Fixed scope: 'men' is not in the 30% or 75% sentences; the 75% is set against 31% of smokers, in the Construction Workers Cohort paragraph.
results.corrected_extracted: Studies by researchers linked to the tobacco industry or sponsored by it were excluded by design, as were estimates based only on combined snus and cigarette use. Exposure caveats: a single baseline recording of tobacco habits; about 30% of exclusive snus users may later stop or move to smoking (a Swedish study cited); in the paragraph on the Construction Workers Cohort, more than 75% of exclusive snus users were under 30 at entry, against 31% of smokers, and only a small proportion of snus users were traced beyond 70; seven of the included studies used construction-worker data from 1971 to 1975, when non-use could not be told from non-response; 13.2% of never-smoking snus users, against 6.7% of never users of tobacco, had a repeat record showing smoking in one study. All authors declare no conflicts of interest; the page has no funding statement.

results.note: Matches Competing interests and Acknowledgements: Swedish Match support, earlier reviews by Philip Morris Products and the European Smokeless Tobacco Council, sponsor not involved, author a long-term industry consultant. '(a snus manufacturer)' is the editors' gloss, not printed in the paper.

Figures match Abstract and Pancreatic cancer paragraphs 1–3; no oesophagus, stomach or lung data in this update, as stated. The source names the comparison for OR 0.98 (never users of tobacco); the anchor did not. Added. No number changes.
results.corrected_extracted: The abstract says the additional evidence extends the list of conditions unassociated with snus (oropharynx, oesophagus, stomach, lung) to include colorectal cancer and acoustic neuroma, and further undermines the weakly-based argument that snus raises pancreatic cancer risk. The text reports no new snus study of pancreatic cancer: a pooled analysis of 11 case-control studies of other smokeless tobacco, none in Scandinavia, gave OR 0.98 (0.75–1.27) for ever use, against never users of tobacco; earlier combined Scandinavian cohorts gave 1.61 (0.77–3.34) in people who never smoked. No oesophageal, stomach or lung data are shown in this update, so their listing rests on the 2011 review, which was not read.

results.corrected_extracted: Case fatality, current against never snus use in male never smokers: in five studies, fatal heart attack RR 1.31 (1.09–1.58) and non-fatal 0.89 (0.79–1.00), ratio 1.48 (1.19–1.84); in the pooled eight-cohort analysis (men who never smoked) incidence RR 1.04 (0.93–1.17) and short-term fatality OR 1.28 (0.99–1.68), with the Construction Workers Study 88% of person-years; the author asks whether the fatality excess is a direct effect or confounding.
